extra.motion: The man in the suit carries on down the iron staircase towards the camera with an easy, pleased swagger, grin fixed, eyes ahead. One hand trails loosely along the rail and slides off at the bottom. He takes the last two steps and plants both feet on the wooden floorboards, squaring his shoulders. The camera stays low on the floor and tilts gently down to follow him as he arrives, keeping him centred, the dark brick wall and raised walkway behind. His footsteps ring on the metal treads, then thud on the wood. Sound: footsteps clanging on iron steps then landing on floorboards, the hollow room tone of a big brick loft, no talking.

The man stays on the spot, facing the same way at the same size in frame, the camera almost motionless. His eyes stay on the people just beside the camera. He says: Two billion pounds. Every teenager in the country, taken round a prison. Scare them straight. As he speaks he spreads both open hands wide on the first words, sweeps one arm out across the room on the second sentence, then chops a hand down firmly on the last, a broad toothy salesman's smile between phrases. The staircase and brick wall behind him stay steady. Sound: his confident male voice, close and clear, over the quiet room tone of a big brick loft.

The man in the balaclava stays seated in the leather armchair, the camera held nearly still. His mask keeps facing the camera, the white ring and the red triangle unchanged. Slowly he tilts his head a few degrees to one side and eases his upper body a few centimetres forward, completely calm and unhurried. On the right armrest, one gloved forefinger lifts gently off the leather and hangs there, as if about to ask something. The rest of him stays utterly still, the factory windows glowing steadily behind. Sound: the soft creak of leather as he shifts, the low room tone of a big brick loft, no talking.

The man stays on the spot at the same size and angle, the camera almost motionless. His wide grin holds for a beat too long while his eyes stay on the people just beside the camera, and the smile slowly stiffens and sets, cheeks rigid, his hands settling still in front of him. Then he recovers and He says: I've got a good feeling. He gives one small, confident nod as he finishes, the grin back in place. The staircase and brick wall behind him do not move. Sound: a moment of near silence in the room, then his upbeat male voice, close, over the quiet room tone of a big brick loft.

The woman in the burgundy suit stays seated in her oxblood armchair, arms still folded, her face at the same size and angle, the camera nearly still. She lowers her chin a fraction and looks out over the top of her half-moon glasses towards the man on the floor beside the camera, eyebrows level, plainly unimpressed. A short pause, then She says: I'm out. Her lips close and she holds the look, unmoved, the factory windows glowing behind her. Sound: her crisp, dry female voice, close and clear, over the low room tone of a big brick loft.

The heavy-set older man in the mustard cardigan starts leaning forward with his hands on his knees, then pushes back and sits back heavily into the leather armchair, his shoulders dropping, his hands sliding off his knees onto the armrests. His face stays facing the same way and keeps roughly the same size in frame as the camera eases back a touch to hold him. Settled, he looks across towards the man on the floor and He says: I'm out. The factory windows glow steadily behind him. Sound: a deep leather creak and the chair taking his weight, then his gruff older male voice, over the room tone of a big brick loft.

She lets her eyes drop to the dark screen of the tablet for a moment, idly, then lifts her gaze back up towards the man on the floor beside the camera, her face returning to the same angle and size as at the start, expression flat and bored. The young nurse stands on the spot with the clipboard pressed to her chest, facing the same way at the same size in frame, the camera nearly still. She draws a small breath, fingers tightening on the clipboard edge, and keeps her eyes on the people just beside the camera. She says: One ward. Six months. If readmissions don't fall by a tenth, you stop paying me. Her voice is slightly nervous at the start but she steadies, giving a small firm nod on the last words and holding her gaze. The staircase and brick wall behind her stay steady. Sound: her young female voice, earnest and clear, over the quiet room tone of a big brick loft.

The man in the balaclava sits completely still in the leather armchair for a long beat, the camera held steady. His mask keeps facing the camera, the white ring and the red triangle unchanged. Then, very slowly, he lifts his gloved hands off the armrests, brings them together in front of him and leans his body forward towards the woman on the floor beside the camera, the move smooth and deliberate, ending close and poised. The factory windows glow steadily behind him. Sound: a long hush, then a slow creak of leather as he leans in, the low room tone of a big brick loft, no talking.

The camera pushes in slowly and smoothly from the floor towards the arc of five armchairs, the tall factory windows glowing behind the panel. Small natural movements around the arc: the woman on the far left shifts her glance; the man in the navy three-piece uncrosses his legs; the man in the mustard cardigan rests a hand on the stack of cash on his glass side table; the woman on the far right taps her tablet. The masked man in the centre stays perfectly still, his mask facing the camera, the white ring and the red triangle unchanged. Sound: the low room tone of a big brick loft, a faint chair creak, a soft rustle of clothing, no talking.
